document.abstract: This paper first briefly summarizes how interactive multimedia services can be implemented in a broadcasting environment characterized by oneway transmission. Next, Integrated Services Television (ISTV) is proposed as an approach for realizing broadcast multimedia services in the digital age. It is shown that the structured data approach is capable of describing displays and services that are flexible and able to be extended. Finally, we assess the effectiveness of ISTV functions and the structured data approach using simulator and test programs. Viewers' responses to a menu display that show a range of available services were solicited, and 90% of the respondents were found to be favorably impressed by the ease with which available services could be understood.

authors.bio: Akira Ohya received his B.E. degree in electric engineering in 1969 and M.E. degree in electric engineering in 1971 from Tokyo University, Japan. He joined NHK in 1971. He has been with the NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories since 1975. Ohya has been working on the development of the still picture broadcasting system, teletext system, data broadcasting system, conditional access system, and ISDB system. He is a senior research engineer of the Multimedia Services Research Division.

He is senior research engineer of the multimedia services research division at NHK Science and Technical Research. Isobe has worked on the development of the teletext, satellite broadcasting, data broadcasting, and the ISDB systems. He is currently in charge of text coding and multimedia coding.
